claims.statement: For n=2p+2+d (d>=1), k=p-1, H_v=T-{v,s_v}, W_v=N_T(s_v)\{v}, an ordering of W_v whose every union N_H[w_i] with earlier mark vertices has size at least d+3 makes the v summand nonpositive. If every v in the fixed F(T,p) has such an ordering, S(T,p)<=0. The source cover-number lower bound is false.
claims.scope: Exact sufficient structural subclass of the primary ordinary-tree setting; no implication from eligibility or favorability to the size condition. Cover bound rejected even for K2.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: first-mark partition and independent-set incidence prove the subclass. K2 with full vertex cover at r=1 has claimed L=-1 but actual Delta_1=-2; the positive a=r+1 cover contribution was replaced by an upper bound. Both critics found this defect.

claims.statement: The fixed-selector deletion-plus-legal-two-for-one weighted clone graph saturates every upper supply under the registered eligible ordinary-tree hypotheses. T2 supplies exact rooted state and weight identities after adding the selected-root-leaf term 1_{r in B}1_{(B-{r}) meets W_r}; T3 proves saturation only for stars in its stated rank range. Universal saturation remains unproved and unrefuted.
claims.scope: Registered universal mechanism is open. Rooted decomposition holds for arbitrary finite ordinary trees with the explicit root-leaf correction; star result has arbitrary fixed F and 2<=p<=m-1, p>(m-1)/2.

The explicit correction restores the identity. No universal Hall cuts, routing, or deficient cut are established; scalar S is weaker.

claims.statement: At n=2p+3, k=p-1, first-mark residuals satisfy |J_i|=2k+3-deg_H(w_i)-i because marks are pairwise nonadjacent. Thus size 2k+2 can arise at (i,deg)=(1,0), size 2k+1 at (1,1) or (2,0), and size 2k at (1,2),(2,1), or (3,0). Residuals of order <=2k-1 have i_k<=i_(k-1); for k edges plus one isolate the difference is 2^(k-2)(4-binomial(k,2)).

The U-critic 23-vertex eligible example has an isolated second mark and a size-2k+1 residual despite ordering a nonisolated mark first; its full S=-44250.

limitations: The universal lower-region ordinary favorable-leaf aggregate is neither proved nor refuted; no eligible positive complete sum appears.
The universal deletion-plus-two-for-one weighted Hall mechanism lacks a cut proof or obstruction; finite scalar sums do not decide it.
The T1 structural condition is not derived from eligibility, and its source cover bound is false.
T4 boundary residuals of orders 2k and 2k+1, including isolated-mark cases, lack general sign or compensation control.
T5 family computation ends at m=50; no infinite selector classification or selected coefficient inequality is proved.
